headword: {多要素認証|たようそにんしょう}

definitions.explanation: A login method that requires two or more independent kinds of proof — a password, a code sent to a phone, a fingerprint — before granting access. Now standard on banking and workplace systems.

examples.japanese: {多要素認証|たようそにんしょう}を{設定|せってい}した。
{社内|しゃない}システムでは{多要素認証|たようそにんしょう}が{必須|ひっす}となった。
examples.english: Multi-factor authentication has become mandatory for internal systems.

examples.japanese: パスワードが{漏|も}れても、{多要素認証|たようそにんしょう}があれば{不正|ふせい}ログインを{防|ふせ}ぎやすい。
examples.english: Even if a password leaks, multi-factor authentication makes unauthorized logins easier to prevent.

notes:
Often abbreviated MFA in Japanese technical writing as well. {二要素認証|にようそにんしょう} (two-factor authentication, 2FA) is the common special case.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {多要素認証|たようそにんしょう}を{導入|どうにゅう}する: to introduce multi-factor authentication
- {多要素認証|たようそにんしょう}を{有効|ゆうこう}にする: to enable multi-factor authentication
- {多要素認証|たようそにんしょう}が{必須|ひっす}: multi-factor authentication is required

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {二段階認証|にだんかいにんしょう}: two-step verification — two steps that may use the same kind of factor, so slightly weaker in principle
- {生体認証|せいたいにんしょう}: biometric authentication — one possible factor within MFA
